Commentary.Commentary: That's a wrap of the two match T20I series between India and West Indies. The men from the Caribbean have won it 1-0 as the second match got washed out. The series was a roller-coaster ride where in one match the batsmen had all the say while the bowlers dominated the other. It was a good venue to host this series and gave the residents of USA the taste of cricket. Let's hope we have many more matches over here in the future. Hope you enjoyed our coverage of this series. Until next time, take care!

West Indies captain, Carlos Brathwaite says that the Indian bowlers bowled very well and executed their plans. Says the game is unpredictable and one never knows what may happen next (Referring to the difference in yesterday's and today's match). (On positives from this series) He says that the positives were the performances from Evin Lewis, Johnson Charles and Dwayne Bravo's bowling at death. Adds that West Indies are Champions and would want to show the world and keep winning. (On the ground) He says it's a fantastic ground and would like to play many more matches over here. Adds that the drainage system will improve and it's going to be one of the bigger venues in the world.

Indian captain, MS Dhoni says it was quite difficult due to weather. (On his team's performance) He praised his bowlers who bowled according to the plans. He said they took one risk of taking Amit Mishra in place of Stuart Binny which meant that they had to play with one batsman short. But, this gamble paid off and worked excellently in their favour. (On this venue) He said it's a good venue to start off some tri-series and play some T20Is over here. It's a win-win situation for everyone as the timings are perfect for a global spectacle and also is a money making venue.
All in all it was an entertaining series for the people in USA who hardly witness any live cricketing action in their country and it was a good platform to make cricket a global sport.

The Indians made one change to their team by bringing in Amit Mishra and it worked wonders. He did exceptionally well by picking up 3 wickets and giving away just 24 runs in his quota of 4 overs. He was well supported by his spin-mate Ravichandran Ashwin, who choked West Indies from one end. Johnson Charles was the only bright spot for the Caribbeans, continuing his previous match heroics and making a quickfire 43.

Sad news folks! PLAY HAS BEEN CALLED OFF officially after just 2 overs were bowled in the second innings. That's a sad ending to the match and the series. India started the chase with a cool and calm head before the rain came pouring down and had the last say in the match. The first innings of the match was a wicket fest contrasting to yesterday's run fest. West Indies were bowled out for 143 within the 20 overs.

UPDATE 2323 IST - The rain has stopped but the outfield has taken a beating. To add to the misery there is no Super Sopper available. Doesn't look good at the moment and the match officials are having a chat in the middle. Stay tuned, we will let you know what happens next.

UPDATE 2240 IST - The rain is coming down steadily. We hope that the rain stops soon and we can continue with the game. One thing is for sure that the overs will start getting reduced from hereon. Stay tuned for further updates!

It has started to drizzle out there and the groundsmen are gearing up. The umpires have asked the players to go back to their respective dressing rooms. We hope that it is just a passing shower as we need a minimum of 5 overs to be bowled for a match to have a result. Remember, the DLS par score for India to win is 27 after 5 overs without any loss of wickets. Stay tuned.
